This work focuses on transaction processing systems (TPS), critical systems operating in high-concurrency environments that execute financial, social, and communicative transactions. Furthermore, the contribution introduces a customized model for the Java Memory Model (JMM), named Test-oriented JMM or ToJMM, designed to render the intricate JMM rules more tractable within the formal environment of the Coq proof assistant. Coq was utilized to develop and confirm the accurate implementation of ToJMM, with a verified thread scheduling and transaction isolation algorithm described whose formal properties guarantee that deadlocks and race conditions cannot occur during testing scenarios. Finally, practical experiments following the formal analysis revealed several deep-seated bugs in popular Java-based libraries used widely for transaction processing.
